newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skanska to sell Sandvik shares worth 10 bln Skr.
newsitem.headline: Skanska to sell Sandvik shares worth 10 bln Skr.

text.p: Swedish construction group Skanska said on Monday it would divest its entire holding in tool and engineering group Sandvik for an amount of around 10 billion crowns.
Skanska to sell Sandvik shares worth 10 bln =3
Skanska said the sale of its Sandvik stake would generate a capital gain of 9.1 billion crowns.
Skanska said it would guarantee the redemption of four billion crowns worth of Sandvik shares proposed by the engineering group.
The redemption price would be based on the average market price of a Sandvik share during May 7-22 application period with a discount of three percent.

"One precondition for Skanska's guarantee, however, is that the redemption price which will be fixed after separation of Sandvik's dividend -- proposed at 6.5 crowns a share -- is not below 170 crowns a share," Skanska said.
"Nevertheless Skanska may carry out its application for redemption even at a lower redemption price."
Skanska said it had agreed to submit a maximum of 23.53 billion Sandvik shares, thereby fully subscribing the offer.
Skanska has further decided to sell 22 million A-series Sandvik shares to investment group Industrivarden at 185 crowns a share for a total of 4.1 billion crowns.
This block of shares is equivalent to 10.2 percent of voting power and 7.9 percent of capital stock in Sandvik.
"Industrivarden has pledged to support the implementation of the share redemption by the board of Sandvik," Skanska said.
Skanska said it had also agreed to sell 10.34 million shares to Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), equivalent to 4.8 percent of vote and 3.7 percent of capital.
These shares were sold at a price of 180 crowns a share totalling 1.8 billion crowns.
"DMG intends to sell these shares as soon as possible to institutional investors in Sweden and internationally," Skanska said.
Skanska shares closed at 324 crowns on Friday.
